recognize_zh: 視野右中處有一顆細胞，細胞質內塞滿多個大小相近、淡色圓形的球狀包涵體（Russell bodies），環繞著偏心的細胞核，呈葡萄串狀，這是含免疫球蛋白堆積的 Mott cell（葡萄細胞）。
features: Single plasma cell with cytoplasm distended by multiple round, pale, uniform globular inclusions (Russell bodies)
Globules arranged around a round nucleus, giving a grape-like or morula appearance
Background marrow with numerous myeloid precursors, band and segmented neutrophils
Scattered plasma cells with eccentric nuclei and pale perinuclear zones
Intense magenta color cast limits assessment of chromatin detail
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular background of maturing granulocytic precursors and neutrophils with scattered plasma cells. One plasma cell contains numerous uniform, round, pale globular cytoplasmic inclusions surrounding the nucleus, consistent with Russell bodies in a Mott cell. The strong magenta color cast of the image limits evaluation of chromatin and cytoplasmic basophilia, and no sheets of atypical plasma cells are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with a Mott cell, which can occur in reactive plasmacytosis as well as in plasma cell neoplasms; correlation with plasma cell percentage and clonality studies is needed.

ddx.dx: Vacuolated cells (e.g. Burkitt lymphoma or monocytes)
ddx.vs: Burkitt cell vacuoles are clear, empty lipid vacuoles in deeply basophilic cytoplasm without a plasma cell nucleus, whereas Russell bodies are solid, faintly staining immunoglobulin globules.
Hemophagocytes are larger with engulfed red cells, platelets or nuclear debris of varying size, not uniform round globules.
Dutcher bodies are single pale immunoglobulin inclusions overlying or invaginating the nucleus, whereas Mott cell globules are multiple and cytoplasmic.
Crystal-storing plasma cells contain needle- or rhomboid-shaped inclusions rather than round globules.
